pages.content:
# Getting Started

Start with an HTTPS request you can repeat from your own application. To reconstruct it, eCapture v2.12.0 needs the TLS implementation that made the connection and the interface that carried its packets.

1. [Check the host and install eCapture](1.1). You can inspect command help before loading a probe.
2. [Identify the TLS implementation](1.2). Choose [OpenSSL/BoringSSL](1.3), [Go crypto/tls](1.4), or [GnuTLS](1.5) and start the corresponding probe before making the request.
3. Read the request and response in the terminal. Add `--output stdout --output session.jsonl` to keep a structured copy alongside the terminal output.

## What changed since v2.8.0

In v2.9.0 the three TLS modules gained a packet-based text source. Since v2.11.0, `--model text` uses that source by default. It combines packets from one interface with the target's TLS secrets and decodes application messages. `--text-source hook` selects the older function read/write events. In v2.12.0 the output flags and receiver protocol changed. See [output destinations and migration](3.5) before moving existing scripts.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Target["TLS library or Go binary"] --> Secrets["TLS secrets"]
    NIC["Selected interface"] --> Packets["TLS packets"]
    Packets --> SDK["Live decryption"]
    Secrets --> SDK
    SDK --> Text["Decoded request or response"]
```

For later analysis, [pcapng mode](3.4) records packets and embedded TLS secrets in one file. [Keylog mode](3.3) supplies secrets for a packet trace recorded separately. [Release history](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/CHANGELOG.md)

# Requirements and Installation

## Check the capture host

Run `uname -m` and `uname -r` on the host or device where the application runs. The collector uses Linux kernel facilities for uprobes and packet capture.

| Release architecture | Kernel minimum | Collector targets |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `amd64` (`x86_64`) | 4.18 | Linux and Android |
| `arm64` (`aarch64`) | 5.5 | Linux and Android |
| `loong64` (`loongarch64`) | 6.6 | Linux |

Linux includes all three TLS modules. Android packages provide `tls` for OpenSSL/BoringSSL and `gotls` for Go TLS applications. [Supported platforms and modules](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/README.md)

## Install a release

Choose the package for your operating system and CPU on the [download page](/en/download/). For example, download the Linux amd64 archive and `checksum-v2.12.0.txt` into the same directory. Check that `sha256sum` prints `OK` for the selected archive before running `tar`.

```bash
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing checksum-v2.12.0.txt
tar -xzf ecapture-v2.12.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
```

In the extracted directory, run `./ecapture --version` and `./ecapture tls --help`. Run subsequent examples with `./ecapture` there, or use `ecapture` after installing it on your `PATH`. Android archives include a device executable. [Package verification](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/release-verification.md)

## Kernel features and privileges

The kernel needs eBPF and uprobe support. CO-RE bytecode uses kernel BTF, normally exposed at `/sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux`. Non-CO-RE bytecode must match the target kernel and be available in the build. A source build on Linux requires Go, Clang/LLVM and the project submodules. Loong64 release builds use LLVM 22.1.8. See [building and selecting bytecode assets](6.1) for build targets. [Build requirements](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/compilation.md)

The capture examples use `sudo`. If you assign capabilities instead, distinguish probes that also attach Traffic Control (TC) programs to a network interface.

| Capture path | Linux 5.8 or later | Earlier supported kernels |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Keylog or explicit `--text-source hook` | `CAP_BPF`, `CAP_PERFMON`, `CAP_SYS_PTRACE` | `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` |
| Native pcapng or default packet-based text | Same capabilities plus `CAP_NET_ADMIN` for TC attachment | `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`, `CAP_NET_ADMIN` |

The default text path and pcapng mode require an active interface carrying the test traffic. Startup logs name the selected interface. Use `-i lo` for a local loopback test, or select the interface in the workload's network namespace. Keep the target library or Go ELF reachable by the collector. [Linux capabilities](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/minimum-privileges.md) · [Interface selection](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/config/capture_interface.go)

# Choosing a TLS Probe

Choose the module by the TLS implementation **inside the application making the connection**. A service written in Go can talk to a client built with GnuTLS. Either endpoint can supply secrets for the same session if its probe supports that implementation.

| Evidence from the application | Module | Target to identify | First capture |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenSSL or BoringSSL, including Android's system BoringSSL | `tls` (alias `openssl`) | Actual `libssl` shared object, optionally set with `--libssl` | [OpenSSL/BoringSSL example](1.3) |
| Go executable uses the standard library's `crypto/tls` | `gotls` (alias `tlsgo`) | The exact executable, required via `--elfpath` | [Go example](1.4) |
| Linux application loads `libgnutls.so` | `gnutls` (alias `gnu`) | Actual GnuTLS shared object, optionally set with `--gnutls` | [GnuTLS example](1.5) |

## Confirm before capturing

- For a curl-based test, `curl -V` reports its TLS backend. Run the check on the capture host, since the developer's copy may use a different backend.
- For a Go service you build, check its metadata with `go version -m /path/to/service` and confirm that the code path under test uses `crypto/tls`. A cgo library can use another TLS implementation.
- When several library versions are installed, select the one loaded by the test application. A matching filename from a different image or installation can refer to another file.

All three modules default to `--model text --text-source pcapng`. Independently choose the interface carrying the packets. If a local service listens on loopback, pass `-i lo`. See [choosing an output mode](3.1) for saved packets or standalone secrets. [TLS command](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/tls.go) · [GoTLS command](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/gotls.go) · [GnuTLS command](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/gnutls.go)

# First OpenSSL and BoringSSL Capture

Use an HTTPS client linked to OpenSSL or BoringSSL and a test endpoint you control. On Linux, check the client with `curl -V`. If it reports GnuTLS, follow the [GnuTLS example](1.5) for that client.

## Start the collector, then make a request

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model text --text-source pcapng
```

The collector searches standard locations for `libssl` and logs the interface it chose. If several OpenSSL builds are installed, pass `--libssl` with the library path used by the client. On Android, use the Android executable and the device's BoringSSL library. The next example selects loopback for a local test server on port 8443.

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model text --text-source pcapng -i lo 'tcp port 8443'
```

In a second terminal, make a new HTTPS connection with a distinctive request path. This example assumes the local test server has a certificate trusted by curl and valid for `localhost`.

```bash
curl --http1.1 https://localhost:8443/ecapture-check
```

## Recognize a decoded message

The probe supplies secrets from your client or server's matching TLS library. The packet capture supplies bytes from the selected interface. eCapture matches them and decodes the HTTP request and response. The terminal event for this test would contain the requested path.

```text
[log_type=event capture_format=text module=tls] GET /ecapture-check HTTP/1.1\x0d
```

Runtime diagnostics have `log_type=log`. If you see only startup logs, check the TLS backend and the interface named in those logs, then open a **new** connection after eCapture is ready. Use `Ctrl+C` to stop. To inspect the same packets later, add `--pcapfile session.pcapng` to the collector command. See [TLS library selection](2.1) and [text output](3.2). [Terminal output format](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/example-outputs.md)

# First GoTLS Capture

Use a Go client or server that you build and that makes HTTPS connections using `crypto/tls`. Choose a request with a recognizable path. You need the same ELF executable used by the running application. An executable from another build may have different function addresses.

## Select the executable and interface

```bash
sudo ecapture gotls --elfpath ./go-client --model text --text-source pcapng
```

Replace `./go-client` with your application path. A PID filter can narrow a capture, but `--elfpath` is still required. The default text source uses TLS secrets from that executable and packets from the selected interface. Specify `-i lo` if the client connects to a server on loopback. To keep a copy of the decoded records, add `--output stdout --output go.jsonl`. [GoTLS command options](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/gotls.go)

## Verify with your workload

1. Wait for the probe to start. In a second terminal run the chosen client, or send an HTTPS request to the selected Go server. Open a fresh connection.
2. Look for an `event` line containing the request path and a response from the same connection. HTTP/2 requests can share a connection, so use the stream ID to pair each request and response.
3. If you see no matching message, check the executable and the interface in the startup log. For a QUIC test, a TCP-only packet filter would exclude the UDP traffic.

To keep the packets and secrets for an independent check, add `--pcapfile go.pcapng` to the same text command and follow the [Wireshark workflow](3.6). To inspect individual function read/write chunks during migration, specify `--text-source hook`. [GoTLS capture](2.2) describes symbol resolution and the three modes. [Output examples](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/example-outputs.md)

# First GnuTLS Capture

On Linux, choose an application linked to a supported version of `libgnutls.so`. For example, use a curl build whose `curl -V` output names GnuTLS. The Android collector omits the `gnutls` command.

## Capture an HTTPS transaction

```bash
sudo ecapture gnutls --model text --text-source pcapng
```

The collector searches common library paths and identifies the patch version to select a matching layout. If the application uses a private installation, pass its actual shared library with `--gnutls /path/to/libgnutls.so.30`. Check the interface named at startup, and use `-i lo` for loopback traffic.

With eCapture running, start the GnuTLS-backed client and request a known path on your test HTTPS server. Use a fresh connection to capture the handshake. The terminal labels decoded records `log_type=event` and `module=gnutls`. Look for the request path and its response. A handshake diagnostic or a growing file alone does not verify decryption.

## Keep the evidence for Wireshark

```bash
sudo ecapture gnutls --model pcapng --pcapfile gnutls.pcapng
```

Run the request again while this capture is active, stop it with `Ctrl+C`, and open the file in Wireshark. To supply keys for a separate packet capture, use `--model keylog --keylogfile gnutls.keys` during the same connection. See the [patch version table](2.3) and [decryption checks](3.6). [GnuTLS command](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/gnutls.go) · [Library detection](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gnutls/config.go)

# Core TLS Modules

The module identifies **where eCapture obtains TLS secrets**. The capture mode identifies **what you get back**. You can use the same text, keylog and pcapng workflows with each supported TLS implementation.

| Module | Target on the capture host | Packet-based text | Explicit hook text |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [tls](2.1) | OpenSSL/BoringSSL shared library on Linux or Android | Library secrets and packets | OpenSSL-style read/write calls |
| [gotls](2.2) | Go `crypto/tls` executable named by `--elfpath` | Go TLS secrets and packets | Go TLS connection reads/writes |
| [gnutls](2.3) | Supported GnuTLS shared library on Linux | GnuTLS handshake secrets and packets | GnuTLS record receive/send calls |

## From a connection to a decoded event

1. Identify the exact ELF binary or shared library used by the workload. Start eCapture before opening the test connection.
2. For the default `--model text --text-source pcapng`, eCapture collects packets on a single interface, associates available secrets and sends a pcapng stream to the live decryption SDK. Set `-i` when the workload uses a different interface from the one selected at startup.
3. The terminal prints decoded messages and runtime logs. To inspect the underlying traffic in Wireshark, add `--pcapfile session.pcapng` or select native `--model pcapng --pcapfile session.pcapng`.

To compare what each mode writes locally and what a downstream receiver gets, see [choosing a capture mode](3.1) and [output destinations](3.5). [Collector reference](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/README.md)

# TLS Capture (OpenSSL and BoringSSL)

`tls` (alias `openssl`) targets the OpenSSL or BoringSSL library used by your application. For a first HTTPS request and an example of the resulting terminal record, see [first OpenSSL and BoringSSL capture](1.3).

## Select the library and version

On Linux, the collector searches common library locations such as distribution directories containing `libssl.so.3` or `libssl.so.1.1`. If the service ships its own library, pass that path with `--libssl`. On Android it also searches Conscrypt APEX and system library directories. An Android application bundling its own TLS implementation can use a different library from the system copy. [Linux library discovery](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/openssl/config_linux.go) · [Android library discovery](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/openssl/config_ecandroid.go)

The probe chooses a bytecode layout for the detected library version. The v2.12.0 table includes patch-specific mappings for the OpenSSL 1.0.2, 1.1.0, 1.1.1, 3.x and 4.0 families, as well as BoringSSL variants. Check the exact patch or Android build when diagnosing a layout mismatch. `--ssl_version` can supply a known version string such as `openssl 3.0.12`. [Version mapping](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/openssl/libs.go) · [Version override](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/tls.go)

## Three ways to observe the same workload

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model text --text-source pcapng
sudo ecapture tls --model keylog --keylogfile openssl.keys
sudo ecapture tls --model pcapng --pcapfile openssl.pcapng
```

Run one command per capture. The first reconstructs messages from packets and TLS secrets. For example, a complete HTTP response can span several packets. The second saves NSS key log lines for a separate trace. The third embeds secrets alongside the packets in a Wireshark-readable file. Packet-based modes choose an interface automatically. Use `-i lo` for a server on loopback. [Output formats](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/event-forward-api.md)

## OpenSSL and BoringSSL capture paths

With `--text-source hook`, the existing `SSL_read` and `SSL_write` paths emit application chunks. With the default packet source, the probe observes TLS secrets and the SDK reconstructs messages. OpenSSL discards premature secret records when the client random is still uninitialized, including sessions reused after `SSL_clear`. Connection metadata used to enrich events stays internal to the probe. [OpenSSL fixes and migration](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/CHANGELOG.md)

For Android BoringSSL builds with mini-debug symbols, the probe can resolve `bssl::ssl_log_secret` from the compressed symbol table. The address has to map into an executable segment of the actual library. [BoringSSL symbol resolution](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/openssl/boringssl_symbol.go)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    ELF["Android libssl ELF"] --> Section[".gnu_debugdata"]
    Section --> Symbols["Decompress inner ELF symbol table"]
    Symbols --> Symbol["Find ssl_log_secret"]
    Symbol --> Offset["Map symbol to executable file offset"]
```

If startup succeeds but no transaction appears, first verify the library, interface and that the connection began after attachment. [Compare the packets and decoded HTTP in Wireshark](3.6) to distinguish a traffic-selection issue from a decryption issue.

# GoTLS Capture

`gotls` (alias `tlsgo`) targets Go's standard `crypto/tls` library in an executable. Point `--elfpath` (`-e`) at the Go client or server you actually run. The ELF architecture must match the collector (`amd64`, `arm64`, or `loong64` on Linux). Use the Android build for a matching Android Go executable on amd64 or arm64. [GoTLS command](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/gotls.go) · [ELF validation](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gotls/config.go)

## Choose the capture path

```bash
sudo ecapture gotls --elfpath ./go-client --model text --text-source pcapng
sudo ecapture gotls --elfpath ./go-client --model keylog --keylogfile go.keys
sudo ecapture gotls --elfpath ./go-client --model pcapng --pcapfile go.pcapng
```

Run the matching executable and make a fresh connection after starting the chosen command. The default text source combines packets with secrets observed at `crypto/tls.(*Config).writeKeyLog`. HTTP events carry the connection and, when available, stream ID needed to follow concurrent requests. Native keylog mode writes NSS secrets. Native pcapng mode records a trace with embedded secrets. In either packet-based path, specify `-i` when the traffic uses loopback or a different route from the default. [GoTLS mode implementation](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gotls/gotls_probe.go)

For a Go HTTP/3 application, include its **UDP** traffic. A filter such as `'tcp port 443'` excludes QUIC. The maintained HTTP/3 fixtures exercise QUIC v1/v2 using Go TLS. Generate traffic for a known endpoint and check the decoded request path and response. See [text decoder and protocol selectors](3.2).

## How the ELF is resolved

The collector reads Go build information and matches function positions in the target ELF. Depending on the build, it can use ELF symbols or Go's function tables, including in PIE binaries. Removing DWARF alone does not determine whether a binary can be traced. The necessary Go metadata and target functions must still be identifiable. Go's pre-1.17 stack convention and newer register ABI use different argument layouts. [ELF and ABI handling](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gotls/config.go) · [Symbol and instruction lookup](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gotls/config_symbol.go)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    ELF["Target executable"] --> Info["Check Go build information and architecture"]
    Info --> Locations["Resolve TLS function locations"]
    Locations --> Secrets["Key-log hook for packet decryption or native secrets"]
    Locations --> Hook["Legacy hook text from connection reads and writes"]
```

Explicit `--text-source hook` uses `crypto/tls.(*Conn).Read` and `crypto/tls.(*Conn).writeRecordLocked` to observe chunks. If your previous integration parsed a PID, direction and bytes from each call, compare the new decoded `TEXT` records against the original request. HTTP/2 streams interleave and socket reads do not define message boundaries. [First GoTLS capture](1.4) includes a verification sequence.

# GnuTLS Capture

`gnutls` (alias `gnu`) observes applications linked to GnuTLS on Linux. The collector locates `libgnutls.so.30` in common system directories. Pass `--gnutls /path/to/libgnutls.so.30` when the target loads a different copy.

## Match the library patch version

GnuTLS handshake structures have version-specific layouts. eCapture reads the version from the library image. If you know the installed patch version, `--ssl_version 3.8.12`, for example, supplies it explicitly. v2.10.0 added measured layouts for GnuTLS 3.8.10–3.8.13. Match the installed patch to the bytecode layout used by v2.12.0.

| Patch range | Bytecode layout selected |
| --- | --- |
| 3.6.12 / 3.6.13–3.6.16 | 3.6.12 / 3.6.13 |
| 3.7.0–3.7.2 / 3.7.3–3.7.6 / 3.7.7–3.7.11 | 3.7.0 / 3.7.3 / 3.7.7 |
| 3.8.0–3.8.3 / 3.8.4–3.8.6 / 3.8.7–3.8.9 | 3.7.7 / 3.8.4 / 3.8.7 |
| 3.8.10 / 3.8.11–3.8.13 | 3.8.10 / 3.8.11 |

The validator rejects versions outside the mapping. A SONAME such as `libgnutls.so.30` can remain the same across many patch versions. Use the actual patch level when checking support. [Full GnuTLS version map](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gnutls/config.go) · [Release notes](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/CHANGELOG.md)

## Capture and verify

```bash
sudo ecapture gnutls --model text --text-source pcapng
sudo ecapture gnutls --model keylog --keylogfile gnutls.keys
sudo ecapture gnutls --model pcapng --pcapfile gnutls.pcapng
```

Choose one command, then open a new connection from a GnuTLS-backed test client. For decoded text, confirm a known request path or response body. For keylog, match the keys against a separate capture of the same connection. For pcapng, open the native file in Wireshark and check that the expected application data decrypts. Set `-i lo` for a client and server communicating over loopback. [Wireshark verification](3.6)

## Handshake and record events

Packet-based text, native keylog and native pcapng obtain secrets at `gnutls_handshake` using the selected layout. A native pcapng file carries these secrets in Decryption Secrets Blocks alongside packet blocks. The default text path streams these blocks to the SDK and emits decoded messages. Explicit `--text-source hook` uses `gnutls_record_recv` and `gnutls_record_send` to deliver chunks from record I/O. [GnuTLS capture implementation](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gnutls/gnutls_probe.go)

# Capture Modes

For `tls`, `gotls` and `gnutls`, `--model` (`-m`) chooses what the collector produces. Start with the question you want the capture to answer. You can inspect the same HTTPS request live, record only its TLS secrets, or save its packet history for Wireshark.

| Question | Mode | What you can verify |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What request did the application send? | [Text](3.2) | Find the decoded path, headers or body in a `TEXT` event. |
| Can I decrypt a trace recorded elsewhere? | [Keylog](3.3) | Load the NSS key log and the matching packets into Wireshark. |
| Which packets carried the request? | [pcapng](3.4) | Follow the decrypted stream in a single file containing packets and secrets. |

## Save and deliver results

`--output` controls terminal, file and TCP destinations for runtime logs and capture events. In native keylog and pcapng modes, use `--keylogfile` or `--pcapfile` to name the required local file. The local `--output` file then contains runtime logs only. In packet-based text mode you may also request either native file while continuing to receive decoded `TEXT` events. [Output contract](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/event-forward-api.md)

- [Choosing text, keylog or pcapng](3.1) compares prerequisites and filenames.
- [Output destinations and subscriptions](3.5) covers Protobuf v2, remote receivers and migration from the v2.8 flags.
- [Wireshark decryption workflows](3.6) shows how to check that the recorded packets and secrets belong to the same test connection.

# Choosing Text, Keylog, or pcapng

## Choose by the artifact you need

| Mode | Input from the workload | Local artifact | What a v2 network receiver gets |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--model text --text-source pcapng` (default) | Packets on one interface and TLS secrets | Optional `--pcapfile` and/or `--keylogfile` | Decoded `TEXT` with available metadata |
| `--model text --text-source hook` | TLS library or Go function I/O | Formatted events via `--output` | `TEXT` from individual calls |
| `--model keylog` | TLS secrets | Required `--keylogfile` in NSS Key Log format | `KEYLOG` with encoded NSS bytes |
| `--model pcapng` | Packets on one interface and TLS secrets | Required `--pcapfile`, optional `--keylogfile` | `PCAPNG` with encoded pcapng bytes |

Every mode also produces runtime logs. In text mode, local `--output` files contain logs and events as Protobuf v2 JSON Lines. In native modes they contain only logs. Keep native paths and JSON Lines paths distinct. [Destination and mode matrix](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/event-forward-api.md)

## Examples for the same OpenSSL request

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model text --text-source pcapng --output stdout --output session.jsonl
sudo ecapture tls --model keylog --keylogfile session.keys
sudo ecapture tls --model pcapng --pcapfile session.pcapng
```

Choose a single command and open the connection after starting capture. For Go workloads, change the command to `gotls --elfpath /path/to/app`. For GnuTLS on Linux, use `gnutls` and supply `--gnutls` when the library is outside the searched paths. Set `-i` if the traffic is on another interface.

## Choose the verification method

- For decoded messages, check the request path and response from the same connection. A socket read can split or combine messages, which affects the explicit hook source.
- For a keylog, collect the packets independently during the same connection. Secrets alone cannot show event order, retransmissions or request contents.
- For a pcapng, open the native file in Wireshark. A trace may contain packets for which no matching secret was collected. Verify a known application message in the decrypted stream.

To view a request immediately **and** retain packets for a later check, add `--pcapfile session.pcapng` to the first command. In that configuration the network event format remains `TEXT`. [Verify decryption in Wireshark](3.6)

# Text Mode

`--model text` reconstructs application messages from packets and TLS secrets. Since v2.11.0, `pcapng` is the default text source for all three core TLS modules. The name describes the **input to the decoder**. A pcapng file is written only when you specify `--pcapfile`.

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model text --text-source pcapng
sudo ecapture gotls --elfpath ./go-client --model text --text-source pcapng
sudo ecapture gnutls --model text --text-source pcapng
```

## Read a message

The decoder reassembles the TCP stream and waits for secrets that can arrive after their packets. It can report complete HTTP/1.x and HTTP/2 messages, supported WebSocket messages, and HTTP/3 over QUIC v1/v2 when the TLS backend supplies the necessary secrets. Include UDP traffic for HTTP/3. With `--text-source hook`, eCapture instead emits the plaintext chunks seen at individual TLS read/write calls. [Live decryption reference](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/README.md#live-decryption-for-text-output)

Each terminal line identifies an event or operational log. A decoded HTTP event includes the available direction, timestamp, endpoints and connection identity. HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 can have multiple streams per connection. Use the stream ID to distinguish them. PID, process name, arguments and non-secret handshake details such as SNI, ALPN and cipher are available when observed. With `--output stdout --output session.jsonl`, the file preserves the v2 structure and its `event_payload.text.payload` is a bytes field encoded as base64 in JSON. [Text output example](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/example-outputs.md)

## Select the decoder for your application

The following options apply to `--model text --text-source pcapng`. Choose one of raw bytes, incremental HTTP events or an explicit application parser.

| Option | When to use it |
| --- | --- |
| `--text-raw` | Inspect authenticated TLS bytes, QUIC STREAM chunks with offsets or complete QUIC DATAGRAM messages. |
| `--text-http-events` | Observe HTTP headers and body chunks as they arrive, including SSE and HTTP/2 gRPC. gRPC payloads retain their schema-free Protobuf bytes. |
| `--text-max-decoded-body N` | With HTTP events, limit gzip expansion to `N` bytes per message. Zero retains compressed data. |
| `--text-protocol dot`, `doh`, `doq`, `mqtt` or `redis` | Select DNS over TLS, HTTPS or QUIC, MQTT 3.1.1, or fixed-length Redis RESP2/RESP3. The selection is explicit. |
| `--text-tls-upgrade` | Follow one `smtp`, `imap`, `pop3`, `ldap`, `postgres`, `mysql`, `connect` or `https-connect` negotiation. Use raw output for subsequent application bytes if there is no parser. HTTPS CONNECT handles one inner TLS layer. |
| `--text-udp-protocol dtls` | Select DTLS 1.2 with ECDHE-RSA and AES-128/256-GCM. UDP normally uses QUIC. |

This example captures incremental gRPC events from a Go service on loopback.

```bash
sudo ecapture gotls --elfpath ./go-server --model text --text-source pcapng \
  --text-http-events -i lo --output stdout --output grpc.jsonl
```

Run a known RPC and check for the expected HTTP/2 stream and message data. A standalone gRPC message has no field names without its `.proto` schema. The current probes do not supply the ECH material needed for live ECH decryption. [Decoder configuration](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/config/decrypt.go) · [Protocol coverage](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/README.md#live-decryption-for-text-output)

## Check what the SDK received

Add `--pcapfile session.pcapng` to keep the bytes sent to the SDK. Add `--keylogfile session.keys` if you also need a standalone key log. Both files are optional and must be distinct from each other and from any JSON Lines output. Check the expected request in Wireshark using [the embedded-secret workflow](3.6). A connection diagnostic can concern just one flow. Unexpected termination of the decryption pipeline stops capture and returns a nonzero exit status. [Decryption and diagnostics](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/output-pipeline.md)

# Keylog Mode

Use `--model keylog` (alias `-m key`) when you already record the network packets separately. eCapture writes the session secrets for the chosen TLS implementation in NSS Key Log format. In v2.12.0 the collector requires an explicit **local** `--keylogfile` (`-k`) path.

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model keylog --keylogfile openssl.keys
sudo ecapture gotls --elfpath ./go-client --model keylog --keylogfile go.keys
sudo ecapture gnutls --model keylog --keylogfile gnutls.keys
```

Start one of these commands and your packet capture before opening a fresh TLS connection. Keylog mode itself does not require a capture interface. If a shared library is in a private installation, identify it with `--libssl` or `--gnutls` as appropriate.

## Recognize and use the key log

Each line consists of a label, the connection's client random, and the corresponding secret, separated by spaces. TLS 1.2 commonly uses `CLIENT_RANDOM`. TLS 1.3 uses separate entries for client/server handshake and application traffic. The placeholders below illustrate the three fields in the native file.

```text
CLIENT_RANDOM <client-random-hex> <master-secret-hex>
CLIENT_HANDSHAKE_TRAFFIC_SECRET <client-random-hex> <secret-hex>
SERVER_TRAFFIC_SECRET_0 <client-random-hex> <secret-hex>
```

A key log has no packet timestamps, ordering or application bytes. In Wireshark's **Protocols → TLS** preferences, set the key log filename for the matching packet trace. Find a request unique to your test. For an equivalent command-line check, see [Wireshark decryption workflows](3.6). Store the key log with the same access controls as the decrypted data. [Keylog format](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/example-outputs.md)

## Delivering the result

`--output runtime.jsonl` saves runtime logs only in this mode. Terminal output labels NSS lines as events in v2.12.0. For remote delivery, TCP and WebSocket publish v2 `KEYLOG` events, and a receiver reconstructs the NSS file from the ordered `keylog.data` bytes. The local `--keylogfile` remains required even when a network receiver is configured. [Receiver contract](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/event-forward-api.md)

# pcapng Mode

Choose `--model pcapng` (alias `-m pcap`) to record packets and their available TLS secrets in a single Wireshark-readable file. Supply an explicit local `--pcapfile` (`-w`). The probe records encrypted packets and embeds the secrets in Decryption Secrets Blocks (DSBs). Wireshark uses those blocks to reconstruct plaintext.

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model pcapng --pcapfile openssl.pcapng
sudo ecapture gotls --elfpath ./go-client --model pcapng --pcapfile go.pcapng
sudo ecapture gnutls --model pcapng --pcapfile gnutls.pcapng
```

## Capture the right interface

Without `-i`, eCapture chooses one active Ethernet interface. It first checks IPv4 and IPv6 default routes and prefers the lowest metric. With no usable default route it prefers the largest RX+TX traffic counter, then an up interface. The startup log reports its choice and reason. Use `-i lo` for loopback, or `--ifname NAME` to select a specific interface. A filter such as `'tcp port 443'` selects HTTPS over TCP. Include UDP when recording HTTP/3. [Interface selection](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/config/capture_interface.go)

Start capture before the handshake, generate a fresh test request, stop the collector, then open the file. Multiple packets may belong to a single decoded message. Unknown process attribution stays unknown. Where observed, the file preserves PID, process name and a capture-time snapshot of up to 256 bytes of process arguments, including a truncation indicator. [Wireshark process fields](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/utils/ecapture.lua)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    NIC["Selected interface"] --> Blocks["Packet blocks"]
    TLS["TLS implementation"] --> DSB["Decryption Secrets Blocks"]
    Blocks --> File["Local pcapng file"]
    DSB --> File
    File --> Trace["Wireshark TLS stream"]
```

## Local files and subscribers

In this example `session.pcapng` holds the native capture and `runtime.jsonl` holds the runtime logs.

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model pcapng --pcapfile session.pcapng --output runtime.jsonl
```

An additional `--keylogfile session.keys` also saves a standalone NSS copy. A terminal destination in v2.12.0 prints runtime logs and labeled byte-count summaries. A local JSON Lines destination gets runtime logs only. TCP and WebSocket carry native `PCAPNG` event bytes. A subscriber that joins late receives a new section and future packets/secrets. To verify decryption, start the client before the test handshake and check a known HTTP message as described in [Wireshark decryption workflows](3.6). [Native files and subscribers](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/event-forward-api.md)

# Output Destinations and Subscriptions

In v2.12.0, `--output` routes runtime logs and captured events. Without the flag, the destination is `stdout`. Explicit destinations **replace** that default. Repeat the flag once per destination to keep two copies.

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model text --text-source pcapng \
  --output stdout --output capture.jsonl
```

## What each destination receives

| Destination | Text mode | Native keylog mode | Native pcapng mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--output stdout` or `stderr` | Labeled logs and decoded text | Logs and labeled NSS lines | Logs and labeled byte-count summaries |
| `--output PATH` or `file:///PATH` | Protobuf v2 JSON Lines, logs and `TEXT` events | JSON Lines, runtime logs only | JSON Lines, runtime logs only |
| `--output tcp://HOST:PORT` | Outgoing JSON Lines with logs and `TEXT` | Logs and `KEYLOG` bytes | Logs and `PCAPNG` bytes |
| `--stream-listen ws://HOST:PORT/PATH` | Incoming subscribers receive binary v2 logs/events | Binary v2 with `KEYLOG` bytes | Binary v2 with `PCAPNG` bytes |

Each terminal line identifies `log_type=log` or `log_type=event`, the module and, for an event, its capture format. In JSON, `PROCESS_LOG` and `EVENT` use the same v2 `LogEntry` schema. Keep native artifact paths separate from `--output` files. [Output API](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/event-forward-api.md)

## Subscribe to the collector

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model text --text-source pcapng \
  --stream-listen ws://127.0.0.1:28256/
```

Connect the receiver to the configured path and negotiate the WebSocket subprotocol `ecapture.v2`. Each binary message contains one Protobuf v2 `LogEntry`. A new subscriber receives a `collector_info` snapshot identifying the host, build, active module, mode, source and destinations, then recent runtime logs and future events. The listener is disabled by default and supplies plain WS without built-in authentication. For eCaptureQ on the same host, enter `ws://127.0.0.1:28256/` as the source. [eCaptureQ quick start](/q/en/quick-start/) [Wire format](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/protobuf/PROTOCOLS.md) · [Receiver example](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/examples/ecaptureq_client/README.md)

TCP output connects to an already-listening receiver. TCP records are newline-delimited JSON. For a native `EVENT`, decode the corresponding `keylog.data` or `pcapng.data` field and append its bytes in order. ProtoJSON base64-encodes bytes. Record boundaries can divide an NSS line or pcapng block.

Starting a new capture generation on reload closes the connections. TCP reconnects, whereas WebSocket clients must resubscribe. Write a fresh receiver file per connection. A late pcapng subscriber gets headers and future packets and secrets only. TCP EOF alone does not confirm completion, so keep interrupted artifacts partial. The collector appends to its local native file across reloads. [Connection and completion rules](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/event-forward-api.md)

## Migrate v2.8–v2.11 commands

| Former option | v2.12.0 change |
| --- | --- |
| `--eventaddr`, `--logaddr`, `-l` | Repeat `--output` for terminal, file and TCP destinations. Update file/TCP readers to decode v2 JSON Lines. |
| Outgoing `ws://` or `wss://` outputs, `--ecaptureq` | Use a v2 WebSocket client connecting to `--stream-listen`, or a JSON Lines receiver for outgoing TCP. |
| `--listen` | Use `--config-listen HOST:PORT` to enable the separate HTTP configuration service. |
| `--eventroratesize`, `--eventroratetime` | Remove both flags. v2.12.0 has no CLI option for file rotation. |
| Implicit keylog/pcapng output or redirected stdout | Specify local `--keylogfile` or `--pcapfile` for the corresponding native mode. |

These legacy options have no aliases. Destinations and listener addresses are fixed at startup. Restart the collector to change them. [v2.12.0 migration details](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/CHANGELOG.md)

# Wireshark Decryption Workflows

Use a request you can identify by its path or response token. Start the collector and any independent packet recorder before making the connection. The result to check is that application message in the decrypted stream.

## Open a capture with embedded secrets

```bash
sudo ecapture tls --model pcapng --pcapfile session.pcapng -i lo 'tcp port 8443'
```

This example assumes your own OpenSSL-backed HTTPS service listens on loopback port 8443. Generate a fresh request and stop eCapture. Open `session.pcapng` in Wireshark, select the test connection and follow the TLS stream. Packet blocks contain the encrypted traffic and DSBs provide the secrets. If you captured with `--model text --text-source pcapng --pcapfile session.pcapng`, the optional file contains the same pcapng stream the live decoder received.

A DSB may arrive after the packets it decrypts. To check the embedded secrets independently with Wireshark tools 4.4 or newer, extract them from this capture into a private temporary file, then preload them while reading it. This example reads TLS stream 0.

```bash
keys=$(mktemp)
editcap --extract-secrets session.pcapng - > "$keys"
tshark -n -r session.pcapng -o "tls.keylog_file:$keys" -q -z follow,tls,ascii,0
rm -f -- "$keys"
```

For a capture containing several TLS connections, choose the target stream. Look for the test token rather than relying on a packet count. [Embedded-secret verification](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/README.md#live-decryption-for-text-output)

## Combine a separate packet capture and key log

1. Start a packet recorder on the interface carrying the test connection, for example `sudo tcpdump -i lo -w network.pcap 'tcp port 8443'`.
2. In a second terminal run `sudo ecapture tls --model keylog --keylogfile session.keys`. Generate the request after both tools are ready. Stop both captures.
3. Open `network.pcap` in Wireshark. In **Preferences → Protocols → TLS**, set the (Pre)-Master-Secret log filename to `session.keys`. Follow the test connection and verify its known request or response.

With TShark, the following command reads TLS stream 0 from the saved trace.

```bash
tshark -n -r network.pcap -o tls.keylog_file:session.keys -q -z follow,tls,ascii,0
```

A key log from another connection or a trace that missed the handshake can leave a flow encrypted. Check the interface, test time and session before changing protocol settings. [Standalone key log example](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/example-outputs.md)

## Inspect process attribution

The optional `utils/ecapture.lua` Wireshark plugin displays PID, process name and capture-time arguments when eCapture recorded them. Argument snapshots can be truncated at 256 bytes. A packet without attribution supplies no process identity. The plugin adds process fields independently of Wireshark's TLS decryption. For a quick view of an HTTP request without opening a trace, use [text mode](3.2). [Wireshark plugin](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/utils/ecapture.lua)

The three core TLS modules share a packet-based text source and a common output interface in v2.12.0. When diagnosing a capture, first identify which interface, library or Go binary, and output destination the collector selected.

| Task | Where to start |
| --- | --- |
| The probe starts but a request is missing | Check the selected interface, the start of the TLS connection, protocol decoding and destination in [TLS troubleshooting](4.1). |
| Send decoded events to another application or change a running probe's filters | Choose an outgoing TCP connection or a WebSocket subscription, and use the separate HTTP configuration API in [Integration and deployment](4.2). |

# TLS Troubleshooting

## The probe fails to start

Check the module's options with `ecapture tls --help` (also available for `gotls` and `gnutls`). Help runs without capture privileges. An unknown `--eventaddr`, `--logaddr` or `--ecaptureq` flag indicates a pre-v2.12 command. See [Integration and deployment](4.2).

| Startup failure | What to check |
| --- | --- |
| Unsupported kernel or architecture | Linux requires x86_64 ≥ 4.18, arm64 ≥ 5.5 or loong64 ≥ 6.6. The Android build targets x86_64 and arm64. |
| Bytecode selection fails | `--btf 0` selects from the embedded objects using detected kernel BTF. CO-RE (`--btf 1`) needs usable BTF and a CO-RE object. An explicit non-CO-RE request (`--btf 2`) needs a non-CO-RE object. Check which variant your binary contains. |
| Permission error during load or TC attachment | Check the collector's eBPF/perf privileges. Both pcapng capture and the default pcapng-backed text source attach TC programs and require network administration privileges on the capture interface. |
| Library, ELF or symbol error | Confirm the program actually uses the selected library. Use `tls --libssl` for OpenSSL/BoringSSL, `gnutls --gnutls` for the GnuTLS library, and `gotls --elfpath` for the application executable. GoTLS attempts Go symbol-table recovery for stripped binaries. Verify the library layout and the reported symbol error before changing build flags. |

[Environment checks](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/env_detection.go) · [Bytecode selection](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/bytecode/selector.go) · [GoTLS symbol resolution](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gotls/config_symbol.go)

## The probe starts, but there is no decoded request

1. **Check the interface.** In text mode the default `--text-source pcapng` needs both packets and secrets. The startup log identifies the selected interface and the reason for the choice. With no `-i`, selection prefers an up Ethernet interface on the lowest-metric default route, then traffic counters or another up interface. For a local loopback workload specify `-i lo`. A single selected interface may miss container or VPN traffic.
2. **Start a fresh test connection.** Start the collector before the handshake and generate one recognizable request from the application you are diagnosing. Check its PID filter and library or executable. A key log without matching packets, or packets without the corresponding secrets, cannot reconstruct the message.
3. **Inspect the optional capture.** In text mode set `--pcapfile sample.pcapng` to keep the same packets and embedded secrets seen by the decoder. Compare the request with [Wireshark](3.6). A pcapng file containing packets alone does not establish that eCapture observed the handshake secrets.
4. **Check the application protocol.** A custom binary protocol may produce no HTTP messages. For packet-backed text, `--text-raw` emits authenticated bytes. For long-running HTTP responses, `--text-http-events` exposes incremental events. `--text-source hook` selects the older, function-call-based representation for comparison and does not require a network interface.

The SDK reports rate-limited connection diagnostics for incomplete or unsupported traffic. Other connections can continue. An unexpected end to the live decoder is a terminal failure. eCapture reports it, releases the probe and exits nonzero. Check the process exit status and the last operational error. [Decryption and diagnostics](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/output-pipeline.md)

# Integration and Deployment

## Migrate a receiver to v2.12

A collector can write to multiple destinations at once. Specify `--output` once per destination, including `stdout` when an operator also needs a terminal copy. Capture data and operational logs share the v2 `LogEntry` schema. Their `log_type` distinguishes `EVENT` from `PROCESS_LOG`.

| Before v2.12 | Current configuration |
| --- | --- |
| `--logaddr` / `-l` and `--eventaddr` | Repeat `--output` for each terminal, file or outgoing TCP destination. Files and TCP use newline-delimited ProtoJSON. |
| `--ecaptureq` or outgoing WebSocket | Use `--stream-listen ws://127.0.0.1:28256/` and have clients subscribe. Upgrade v1 receivers to the v2 schema. Outgoing TCP remains available for push-based receivers. |
| `--listen` | Use `--config-listen HOST:PORT` for the HTTP configuration service. |
| `--eventroratesize` / `--eventroratetime` | Remove the rotation flags from service definitions. v2.12 has no CLI equivalent. |

For example, this configuration keeps a local console and JSON Lines copy of decoded text and opens a subscription endpoint. Both listeners are disabled until explicitly configured. The WS and HTTP services have no built-in TLS or application authentication. Bind them to loopback or an access-controlled network.

```sh
sudo ecapture tls --model text --text-source pcapng \
  --output stdout --output capture.jsonl \
  --stream-listen ws://127.0.0.1:28256/ --config-listen 127.0.0.1:28258
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Collector"] -->|"--output stdout"| B["Labeled terminal"]
    A -->|"--output path"| C["JSON Lines file"]
    A -->|"Outgoing TCP"| D["JSON Lines receiver"]
    E["eCaptureQ or another client"] -->|"Connect to --stream-listen"| A
    A -->|"Binary v2 records"| E
    F["HTTP configuration client"] -->|"POST to --config-listen"| A
```

A TCP receiver accepts the collector's connection and buffers complete lines before decoding. WebSocket clients connect to the collector, negotiate `ecapture.v2` and decode one binary `LogEntry` per message. A new subscription receives a heartbeat, a `collector_info` snapshot, recent operational logs and live events. Use the snapshot to identify the host, build, module, mode and selected outputs. There is no event replay. [Protocol reference](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/protobuf/PROTOCOLS.md) · [Go receiver](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/examples/ecaptureq_client/README.md)

## Native artifacts and reconnection

In keylog mode pass a local `--keylogfile`. In pcapng mode pass a local `--pcapfile`. Keep these paths separate from each JSON output file, which contains only operational logs in those modes. TCP and WebSocket receivers can reconstruct the native artifact. Decode the matching event and append its `keylog.data` or `pcapng.data` bytes in delivery order. A message boundary can fall inside a line or a pcapng block.

Reload drains and closes the old generation's network connections. TCP output reconnects and WebSocket clients must resubscribe. Start a fresh receiver file per connection. A late pcapng subscriber gets fresh section and interface headers and only subsequent packets and secrets. For WebSocket check successful drain, normal close (1000) and local framing/flush before finalizing the file. TCP EOF carries no completion status. Keep the file partial until an external signal confirms completion. [Output and subscription API](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/event-forward-api.md)

## Change capture settings at runtime

Send `POST` requests with a JSON body to the endpoint for the active probe. Routes are `/tls`, `/openssl` and `/boringssl` for OpenSSL/BoringSSL, `/gotls` for Go TLS, and `/gnutls` for Linux GnuTLS. The body replaces the capture configuration. Resend filters, paths and mode settings you need to retain. The following replacement keeps a local GoTLS workload on the loopback interface.

```json
{"elf_path":"/opt/demo/go-client","capture_mode":"text","text_source":"pcapng","ifname":"lo"}
```

The collector rejects output routes, listener addresses and legacy routing fields in a core-module update, including an explicit `null`. Restart the process to change those settings. Reusing a native path appends the new generation locally. Use a new path for a separate capture.

| HTTP result | Interpretation |
| --- | --- |
| 200, code 0 | The replacement probe started. |
| 400, code 4 | The body failed to decode, used a forbidden routing field or selected an unavailable configuration factory. |
| 400, code 5 | Validation or the generation switch failed. Validation preserves the running probe. If startup fails after the switch began, check whether rollback restored it. |
| 503, code 6 | The update queue is full. Retry after backoff. |

# TLS Capture Architecture

## From attachment to capture

The CLI creates a concrete probe through the factory. Each module chooses its library or binary and sets up an eBPF manager with matching attachments, maps and decoders. `BaseProbe` supplies tracked readers and dispatch. The capture mode **and** text source determine which records the manager needs.

| Mode / source | Collected records | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` with `pcapng` (default) | TC packets on the selected interface and TLS secret events from the target | A live pcapng stream feeds the decryption SDK. It emits reconstructed messages or explicitly selected protocol events. |
| `text` with `hook` | TLS read/write function events | Individual plaintext reads/writes through the compatibility path. |
| `keylog` | TLS secret events | Deduplicated NSS key log lines. |
| `pcapng` | TC packets and TLS secret events | Packets and Decryption Secrets Blocks in a pcapng file. |

The gradual deprecation applies to hook-based **plaintext**. The default packet-backed text path still consumes secret events produced by the library/runtime probes. [Architecture](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/architecture.md) · [Output paths](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/output-pipeline.md)

## Library and symbol resolution

- **OpenSSL/BoringSSL.** The `tls` module selects eBPF objects with offsets for the detected library version. Its private connection records enrich applicable data events before dispatch. Secret capture rejects incomplete OpenSSL snapshots when the client random has not yet been initialized, including session reuse after `SSL_clear`. [OpenSSL implementation](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/openssl/openssl_probe.go) · [Release history](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/CHANGELOG.md)
- **Go TLS.** The probe resolves functions in the selected executable, handles Go's stack and register calling conventions and uses Go symbol data when ELF symbols are missing. The selected mode determines whether it needs plaintext read/write or secret-writing sites. [GoTLS symbol resolution](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gotls/config_symbol.go) · [GoTLS implementation](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gotls/gotls_probe.go)
- **GnuTLS.** The detected version selects a measured object layout. The mapping includes 3.8.10 and reuses the 3.8.11 object for upstream 3.8.12 and 3.8.13. The version check runs before attachment. [GnuTLS configuration and asset map](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gnutls/config.go)

## The C/Go boundary

Kernel event records are a binary ABI. The reader chooses a module decoder by eBPF map. Field order, signedness, widths, padding and byte order must agree between C and Go. For example, the GoTLS **hook** event `go_tls_event` is decoded little-endian.

| Wire offset | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| 0–15 | 64-bit monotonic timestamp, then 32-bit PID and TID |
| 16–27 | Signed 32-bit data length, one-byte event type, three padding bytes and a 32-bit file descriptor |
| 28–67 | Source and destination addresses (16 bytes each), ports, IP version and alignment bytes |
| 68–83 | 16-byte process name |
| 84 onward | Payload. The decoder checks the declared length against both remaining bytes and the 16 KiB limit. |

Packet-mode events have a different ABI. The TC event carries process identity and, when available, a bounded argument snapshot. The pcapng writer preserves endpoint attribution with the packet and stores argv in an Enhanced Packet Block comment. Downstream decoded events can then retain PID, process name and up to 256 bytes of arguments with an explicit truncation flag. Unknown ownership stays unknown. [GoTLS C layout](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/kern/gotls_kern.c) · [Go decoder](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gotls/event.go) · [Packet metadata](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/output-pipeline.md)

# Probe Framework and Lifecycle

## Registration and startup

The CLI imports each module's probe package. Its `register.go` initializer registers a factory constructor. `runProbe` validates the selected module configuration, calls `factory.CreateProbe`, and invokes `Initialize` and `Start`. Configuration validation must be idempotent because initialization may validate it again.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as CLI
    participant P as Concrete probe
    participant B as BaseProbe
    participant M as eBPF manager
    C->>P: Initialize(ctx, config)
    P->>B: Validate configuration and prepare dispatcher
    C->>P: Start(ctx)
    P->>B: Select embedded bytecode
    P->>M: Initialize maps and programs, then attach
    M-->>P: Event maps
    P->>B: Register handlers and start tracked readers
```

`BaseProbe` owns shared dispatch, readers and the optional perf-reorder window. Concrete probes own their manager, attachments, map-to-decoder mappings and mode-specific handlers. The CLI owns the configured outputs and listeners and supplies them to the active probe. [Architecture and ownership](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/architecture.md) · [BaseProbe](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/base/base_probe.go)

## Readers and ordering

Each active map needs both a matching decoder and a running reader. `StartPerfEventReader` and `StartRingbufReader` track their read loops independently. With perf reordering enabled, a supported decoder/event pair supplies the original monotonic timestamp. Readers can then sort within a bounded lag window. Multiple readers may still invoke a shared handler concurrently. Preserve synchronization in encoders and writers.

## Reload, failure and close

An HTTP reload constructs a fresh configuration of the same probe type. After validation, the CLI stops the old generation before starting the next one. A failed start triggers an attempt to restore the previous configuration. TCP and WS connections end at a generation boundary while process-level destination settings persist. The client may see a gap between generations. [HTTP update contract](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/remote-config-update-api.md)

If the live decryption stream terminates unexpectedly, the first terminal error wakes the CLI through `BaseProbe.Fail`, even on idle input. Cleanup stays with the CLI. The concrete probe detaches its manager and releases module-owned resources. `BaseProbe.Close` unblocks the readers, waits for their goroutines (including pending reorder work), and only then closes the dispatcher and its handlers. This ordering allows accepted packets and secrets to drain during normal shutdown. A terminal write or drain failure is returned to the caller. [Reader shutdown](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/base/base_probe.go) · [Decoder failure and drain](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/output-pipeline.md)

# Event and Output Pipeline

## Dispatch from the kernel

A perf or ring-buffer reader passes a sample to its registered `EventDecoder.Decode`. The decoder may implement `EventPreprocessor` to consume private records, such as OpenSSL connection bookkeeping. For public domain events, `events.Dispatcher` validates the event and synchronously calls each handler whose `Supports` method accepts it. Handler order is unspecified. Multiple readers may dispatch concurrently. The standalone `pkg/event_processor` is outside this production path. [Dispatcher](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/events/dispatcher.go) · [Reader and handler contracts](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/probe-development.md)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    R["Perf / ring-buffer sample"] --> D["Module decoder and preprocessor"]
    D --> E["events.Dispatcher"]
    E --> P["Packet and TLS secret handlers"]
    P --> S["Serialized pcapng session"]
    S --> SDK["Live decryptor"]
    SDK --> T["TEXT publisher"]
    E --> H["Hook text handler"]
    H --> T
    S --> N["Native pcapng encoder output"]
    E --> K["NSS key log encoder"]
    K --> B["Native file and network EVENT"]
    N --> B
```

## Encoding and ownership

In the default text path, a low-latency pcapng session feeds packets and Decryption Secrets Blocks into the SDK through a pipe. The SDK matches secrets, reassembles flows and calls back with decoded messages. The callback publishes `TEXT` even when a local copy of the pcapng stream is saved. Explicit hook text formats the underlying read/write event directly.

The keylog handler deduplicates secrets and writes normalized NSS lines. A pcapng session copies packet/key material before queueing it and serializes encoder writes. A keylog adapter can flush pending DSBs into the session. On close, the handler drains pending secrets and packets, flushes the encoder and closes its owned sink. The adapter borrows the session. It must leave final close to the owner. [Output architecture](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/output-pipeline.md) · [Keylog handler](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/base/handlers/keylog_handler.go)

## Where v2 records go

`writers.ByteSink` provides `Write`, `Name`, `Flush` and `Close` for byte-oriented destinations. The CLI owns publishers for the life of the process. Probe generations borrow them. The WS subscription server implements typed operational-log and captured-event interfaces and lives in `internal/output/stream`. Receiver code can import the public `github.com/gojue/ecapture/v2/protobuf/gen/v2` types.

| Destination | Data representation |
| --- | --- |
| Terminal | Readable, labeled lines. In v2.12.0 a pcapng event is displayed as a byte-count summary. |
| File via `--output` | One ProtoJSON record per line. Captured events are included in text mode. In keylog/pcapng mode the JSON file contains operational logs only. |
| TCP via `--output` | One ProtoJSON record per line, including native events for keylog/pcapng. |
| WebSocket via `--stream-listen` | One binary v2 `LogEntry` per message. Clients negotiate the `ecapture.v2` subprotocol. |
| Native local file | `--keylogfile` and `--pcapfile` hold the actual NSS/pcapng bytes. |

For a captured `EVENT`, match `event_payload.capture_format` to its `text`, `keylog` or `pcapng` member. Preserve available process arguments, truncation status, network tuple and TLS observations when forwarding `TEXT`. For native events append the decoded bytes in order for that connection. The packet writer may split a block across records. On reload, the collector drains and ends that generation's network connections. See [receiver completion and reconnection](4.2). [Protocol reference](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/protobuf/PROTOCOLS.md)

# Extending a TLS Probe

## Keep the attachment map and decoder in sync

A change to an existing TLS probe crosses the boundary between the eBPF object and the Go manager. Check the C section, BPF function and map name against the manager's section, function and map registration. Resolve the target against the actual library or Go executable. A map with a decoder also needs a tracked reader. For fields crossing this boundary, keep exact widths, signedness, byte order, padding and length validation aligned. Exercise short, malformed, maximum-size and valid padded samples. Per-CPU reordering relies on the original monotonic timestamp. [Probe development guide](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/probe-development.md)

## Version-specific bytecode

OpenSSL patch versions may share a measured layout. Check the version-to-object mapping in `sslVersionBpfMap` and confirm both CO-RE and non-CO-RE variants can resolve the intended base name. GnuTLS 3.8.10 and 3.8.11 have separate layouts, while 3.8.12 and 3.8.13 map to the 3.8.11 object. GoTLS resolves its functions in the selected executable. A new library layout needs a capture test with that library, in addition to a mapping test. [OpenSSL mappings](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/openssl/libs.go) · [GnuTLS mappings](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gnutls/config.go) · [Go symbol resolver](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/gotls/config_symbol.go)

A change to secret extraction affects default text, keylog and native pcapng. Test reconstructed output during a live request, independent decryption with the saved NSS file, and decryption using only the pcapng's embedded DSBs. Test the legacy hook source separately when read/write records change. For GnuTLS, the manager routes both packet-backed text and pcapng mode through the packet capture setup. For cross-builds, prepare the **target** kernel headers and configuration and point `KERN_HEADERS` at that tree. Native non-CO-RE builds normally use the running kernel's build/source tree. LoongArch CO-RE requires target BTF to generate its `vmlinux.h`. [Toolchain and recipes](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/compilation.md) · [Architecture selection](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/variables.mk) · [LoongArch details](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/loong64-support.md)

## From C objects to the executable

```text
kern/*.c
  -> .build/<target>-<goarch>/bytecode/*_kern_{core,noncore}.o
  -> assets/ebpf_probe_<target>_<goarch>_bindata.go
  -> .build/<target>-<goarch>/bin/ecapture
  -> bin/ecapture
```

`make core` embeds only CO-RE objects, `make nocore` only non-CO-RE objects, and `make all` includes both. CO-RE uses type information for relocation. The non-CO-RE recipe compiles against prepared kernel headers, including handling for Linux 6.19+ anonymous fields and Linux 7.x x86 headers. Both recipes strip DWARF with `llvm-strip -g` and retain BTF. The runtime selector matches the requested BTF mode to the objects present in the resulting binary. [Object recipes](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/Makefile) · [Runtime selector](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/probe/bytecode/selector.go)

Run the native build in the prepared Linux checkout.

```sh
git submodule update --init --recursive
make clean
make env
make all
file bin/ecapture
```

The Makefile builds libpcap for the selected target and links it through CGO. An `ebpfassets` build uses generated assets, and `ecap_android` selects the Android module set. A plain Go build can select the asset stub, which cannot load a probe. The final link verifies static PIE, no ELF interpreter and no shared-library dependencies before copying the executable to `bin/ecapture`. [Go build and link checks](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/functions.mk) · [Build tags and production verification](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/build-test.md)

# TLS Test and E2E Strategy

## What each test verifies

Unit tests run decoders against short, padded and maximum-size samples and check module configuration and version mappings. On Linux, `go test -v -race ./...` checks the default-tag build. To exercise production code, generate actual bytecode with `make all` and use `make test-race`. The production-tag lint command also needs the target's built libpcap. [Build and test guide](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/agent/build-test.md)

The maintained Linux E2E harness runs on Ubuntu 22.04+ or Debian 13+ with root and an eBPF-capable kernel. It uses deterministic local clients and an independent Wireshark decoder. Install both `tshark` and `editcap` 4.4+ for the pcapng/QUIC checks, plus OpenSSL and GnuTLS development headers for the C workloads.

```sh
make all
sudo make e2e-linux
# Focus on the two GoTLS artifact modes.
sudo env E2E_MODULES=gotls E2E_MODES='keylog pcapng' bash test/e2e/run_e2e.sh
```

| Mode under test | Evidence required |
| --- | --- |
| Default text | The expected request or response appears while capture is running. The harness checks TLS 1.2 and 1.3 and independently decrypts the optional pcapng using embedded secrets. Hook-specific tests select `--text-source hook`. |
| Keylog | The local NSS file contains usable TLS 1.2 and 1.3 secrets that decrypt an independently collected packet capture. |
| Pcapng | The local file contains section/interface headers, packets and TLS Decryption Secrets Blocks. Decryption must work with its embedded secrets. |
| Output and reload | Each Linux core module exercises labeled stdout, JSON Lines file/TCP destinations, binary v2 subscriptions and same-probe HTTP reload. In native modes a file `--output` must contain only operational logs. |

## Protocol and platform coverage

GoTLS tests include segmented HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 bodies, HTTP/3 over QUIC v1/v2, raw binary TLS, DNS over TLS/HTTPS/QUIC and incremental SSE/gRPC. The HTTP/3 baseline checks two concurrent connections with two streams each and independently decrypts their bodies. It does not establish coverage of migration, 0-RTT or all QUIC states. OpenSSL checks bidirectional TLS 1.3 KeyUpdate, DTLS 1.2 ECDHE-RSA AES-GCM and connection reuse after `SSL_clear`. The GnuTLS keylog tests require both TLS versions to decrypt.

Android E2E uses a Linux host and a rooted API 33+ device/emulator. Its client uses platform Conscrypt/BoringSSL and sends a gated HTTPS request after the probe is ready. CI covers API 33–36. Native LoongArch E2E runs the OpenSSL and GoTLS CO-RE workloads on a dedicated Debian host. The non-core shell/database suite has separate entry points and its older output checks are outside the v2 transport gate. [Maintained E2E matrix and entry points](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/test/e2e/README.md) · [Linux workflow](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/.github/workflows/e2e.yml) · [Android workflow](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/.github/workflows/android_e2e.yml)

# CI, Packaging, and Release

## Pull requests and capture tests

The upstream `GO/C/C++ CI` workflow builds on Ubuntu 22.04 amd64 and arm64, checks CO-RE and non-CO-RE builds, compiles cross-target variants, runs lint and executes `go test -v -race ./...`. CodeQL analyzes the Go and C/C++ sources separately. PR debug packaging uses Ubuntu 24.04 jobs and the same `TARGET_ARCH` initializer as the release workflow. Its tarballs preserve the executable inside the archive. [Build CI](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/.github/workflows/go-c-cpp.yml) · [CodeQL](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/.github/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml) · [Debug packages](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/.github/workflows/pr_build_debug.yml)

The Linux capture matrix uses hosted Ubuntu 22.04 and 24.04 runners for OpenSSL, GoTLS and GnuTLS. Trusted changes also run OpenSSL and GoTLS CO-RE on a native Debian LoongArch64 runner. This job verifies the event commit and binary architecture, attaches probes to the real kernel, and cleans its capture files even on failure or cancellation. It retains the test log for seven days. Android runs its own Conscrypt/BoringSSL workload. See [TLS tests and E2E strategy](6.2). [Linux E2E workflow](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/.github/workflows/e2e.yml) · [Android E2E workflow](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/.github/workflows/android_e2e.yml)

## What a release tag produces

A `v*` tag starts parallel Ubuntu 24.04 build jobs for `amd64`, `arm64` and `loong64`. Each selects its architecture with `TARGET_ARCH`, prepares the target headers and runs the release Makefile. Successful jobs upload validated artifacts for the publish job.

| Architecture | Expected files |
| --- | --- |
| amd64, arm64 | Linux tarball and Debian package, plus an Android tarball containing the executable. These packages are required before publishing. |
| loong64 | Linux tarball and Debian package. The build also audits the LoongArch toolchain and result. If this optional build fails, its files are omitted from that release. |

The publish job merges the uploaded artifacts, checks the required packages, generates the release checksums and publishes the GitHub Release. It then extracts the **same** amd64 and arm64 Linux executables from the published tarballs into the Docker build context. BuildKit selects the binary matching `TARGETARCH` for each image. Both architectures get the version tag, and stable releases also update `latest`. [Release workflow](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/.github/workflows/release.yml) · [Release Makefile](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/builder/Makefile.release) · [Container recipe](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/builder/Dockerfile)

pages.content:
# 快速入门

先用自己的应用发起一次可重复的 HTTPS 请求。要让 eCapture v2.12.0 还原这次请求，需要先确认应用使用的 TLS 实现，以及承载流量的网卡。

1. [检查环境并安装 eCapture](1.1)。加载探针前即可查看命令帮助。
2. [确认 TLS 实现](1.2)。根据应用选择 [OpenSSL/BoringSSL](1.3)、[Go crypto/tls](1.4) 或 [GnuTLS](1.5)，先启动相应的探针，再发起请求。
3. 在终端查看请求和响应。如需同时保留结构化记录，可以追加 `--output stdout --output session.jsonl`。

## 从 v2.8.0 升级

v2.9.0 为三个 TLS 模块增加了基于网络包的文本数据源。从 v2.11.0 起，`--model text` 默认使用这一数据源，把单张网卡上的数据包与目标程序的 TLS 密钥配对，再解码应用消息。需要沿用原来的函数读写事件时，显式指定 `--text-source hook`。v2.12.0 更改了输出参数和接收协议，迁移脚本前可查看[输出目的地与迁移说明](3.5)。

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Target["TLS 库或 Go 程序"] --> Secrets["TLS 密钥"]
    NIC["指定网卡"] --> Packets["TLS 数据包"]
    Packets --> SDK["实时解密"]
    Secrets --> SDK
    SDK --> Text["还原的请求或响应"]
```

需要离线分析时，[pcapng 模式](3.4)可以将网络包和密钥写入同一文件。已有独立抓包的场景，可以用[密钥日志模式](3.3)取得同一会话的密钥。[上游版本记录](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/CHANGELOG.md)

# 环境要求与安装

## 检查采集主机

在运行应用的主机或设备上执行 `uname -m` 和 `uname -r`。采集器依赖 Linux 内核的 uprobe 与网络抓包能力。

| 发布包架构 | 最低内核 | 采集平台 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `amd64`（`x86_64`） | 4.18 | Linux、Android |
| `arm64`（`aarch64`） | 5.5 | Linux、Android |
| `loong64`（`loongarch64`） | 6.6 | Linux |

Linux 版本包含全部三个 TLS 模块。Android 包提供用于 OpenSSL/BoringSSL 的 `tls` 和用于 Go TLS 程序的 `gotls`。[平台与模块支持列表](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/README.md)

## 安装发布包

从[下载页](/zh/download/)选择与操作系统、CPU 匹配的包。例如，将 Linux amd64 压缩包和 `checksum-v2.12.0.txt` 下载至同一目录，在执行 `tar` 前，先确认 `sha256sum` 对所选包输出 `OK`。

```bash
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing checksum-v2.12.0.txt
tar -xzf ecapture-v2.12.0-linux-amd64.tar.gz
```

在解压后的目录中运行 `./ecapture --version` 和 `./ecapture tls --help`。后续示例可在该目录使用 `./ecapture`，或将可执行文件安装到 `PATH` 后使用 `ecapture`。Android 压缩包包含可在设备上运行的程序。[发布包校验说明](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/release-verification.md)

## 内核特性与权限

内核需支持 eBPF 和 uprobe。CO-RE 字节码使用内核 BTF，通常可在 `/sys/kernel/btf/vmlinux` 找到。使用非 CO-RE 字节码时，构建产物中需要包含与目标内核匹配的对象文件。在 Linux 上从源码构建还需 Go、Clang/LLVM 及项目子模块。Loong64 发布包使用 LLVM 22.1.8。各编译目标见[构建与字节码资源](6.1)。[上游编译说明](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/compilation.md)

教程使用 `sudo` 运行采集。如果采用 Linux capabilities 单独授权，需要区分采集方式是否在网卡上挂载流量控制（TC）程序。

| 采集路径 | Linux 5.8 及以上 | 更早的受支持内核 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 密钥日志或显式 `--text-source hook` | `CAP_BPF`、`CAP_PERFMON`、`CAP_SYS_PTRACE` | `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` |
| 原生 pcapng 或默认的网络包文本解密 | 同上，另需挂载 TC 所用的 `CAP_NET_ADMIN` | `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`、`CAP_NET_ADMIN` |

默认文本模式和 pcapng 模式均需要一张承载测试流量的活动网卡。启动日志会显示选中的网卡。本地回环测试指定 `-i lo`，容器内流量要选用工作负载所在网络命名空间的网卡。采集器还须能够访问目标程序使用的库或 Go ELF 文件。[Linux 权限要求](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/docs/minimum-privileges.md) · [网卡选择逻辑](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/internal/config/capture_interface.go)

# 选择 TLS 探针

根据**建立 TLS 连接的应用实际使用的 TLS 实现**选择探针。例如 Go 服务可以处理 GnuTLS 客户端发来的请求。只要探针支持对应的实现，在任一端获取的密钥都可以用于该会话。

| 应用特征 | 模块 | 需要确认的目标 | 首次采集 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OpenSSL 或 BoringSSL，包括 Android 系统 BoringSSL | `tls`（别名 `openssl`） | 应用实际使用的 `libssl` 共享库，可通过 `--libssl` 指定 | [OpenSSL/BoringSSL 示例](1.3) |
| Go 可执行文件使用标准库 `crypto/tls` | `gotls`（别名 `tlsgo`） | 通过必填的 `--elfpath` 指定目标可执行文件 | [Go 示例](1.4) |
| Linux 应用加载 `libgnutls.so` | `gnutls`（别名 `gnu`） | 实际加载的 GnuTLS 共享库，可通过 `--gnutls` 指定 | [GnuTLS 示例](1.5) |

## 采集前确认

- 用 curl 做测试时，`curl -V` 会显示其 TLS 后端。请在采集主机上检查，开发机上的 curl 可能使用不同的 TLS 库。
- 对于自行构建的 Go 服务，可以用 `go version -m /path/to/service` 检查构建信息，再确认测试代码路径使用 `crypto/tls`。通过 cgo 调用的库可能使用其他 TLS 实现。
- 如果安装了多个版本的库，请指定测试应用实际加载的文件。另一个容器镜像或安装目录中可能存在同名但不同的库。

三个模块都默认使用 `--model text --text-source pcapng`。还需要单独确认承载数据包的网卡，例如本地回环服务使用 `-i lo`。如果需要保留密钥或数据包，参见[捕获模式选择](3.1)。[TLS 命令](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/tls.go) · [GoTLS 命令](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/gotls.go) · [GnuTLS 命令](https://github.com/gojue/ecapture/blob/v2.12.0/cli/cmd/gnutls.go)
